_comment: Source of truth for Wren's App Store listing in its primary language.
Every other locale is translated from this file, so edit it here and
re-run the push rather than editing anything in App Store Connect by hand.
Apple's limits: name 30, subtitle 30, promotionalText 170, keywords 100,
description 4000. The push script checks all of them before sending.
Shared fields — name and the two URLs — come from common.json.
subtitle: Place lists into map guides
promotionalText: Seamlessly turn curated lists of places into one guide on your map: off a screenshot, out of a file another app exported, or from a guide you already keep.
description:
Someone sends you a reel. Five places you have to eat at in Rome, a rooftop bar in Lisbon, a bookshop down an alley in Tokyo. You mean to remember. By Thursday it is gone.

Wren catches them — off a screenshot, out of a list another app exported, or from a guide you already keep — and puts them where you will be standing when you need them.

THREE WAYS IN

Places do not only arrive as screenshots, so there are three ways to hand them over. All of them end in the same place: a guide in Apple Maps.

1. FROM SCREENSHOTS. One tap per place, from a reel, a post, a message from a friend, or a photographed page of a guidebook. Text recognition runs on your phone, so the screenshots stay there. Wren also reads the caption to work out which city you are looking at, and asks you to confirm it.

2. FROM A FILE. A list exported from another app — CSV, KML, KMZ, GPX, GeoJSON, or a Google Takeout export of your saved places. Where the file carries coordinates, each place is looked up near its own, so a list spanning three cities resolves correctly rather than being dragged towards one of them.

3. FROM A GUIDE YOU ALREADY HAVE. Share a guide out of Apple Maps, paste the link into Wren, and it reads the places already in it. Newly found places sit alongside them, and one guide is made holding both.

THEN YOU CHECK IT

Every place shows what was read beside what was matched, so a wrong match is obvious rather than confident. Anything not found — or found wrongly — can be searched again by hand. Nothing is written to Apple Maps until you say so.

What comes out is not a copy of your places in another app. It is an actual guide, in the Maps you already use, on every device signed in to your Apple Account. About a hundred and fifty places fit in one guide; beyond that Wren splits them into numbered guides and tells you before it does, rather than quietly dropping the ones that would not fit.

ANYWHERE, NOT JUST RESTAURANTS

Restaurants and bars, certainly. Also viewpoints, markets, hotels, galleries, shops, trailheads, beaches and the odd petrol station someone insists does the best coffee for fifty miles. Anywhere with a name and a location.

NO ACCOUNT, NO SIGN-IN

Wren has no account and reads nothing from yours. Your screenshots are read on your device and are never uploaded, and Wren does not connect to Instagram or any other service — it sees only the screenshots and files you choose to give it.

Two things leave your phone, both small and both necessary: the name of a place, sent to Apple Maps so it can be found, exactly as the Maps app does; and, if you paste a shared guide link, that link, sent to Apple to be expanded. Entering a complimentary access code is the only time Wren contacts a server of its own.

FREE, WITH ONE OPTIONAL PURCHASE

Guides of up to three places are free, for good. Two things are a single one-time purchase: saving a guide with more than three places, and adding to a guide you already have. No subscription, nothing that renews, and it restores on your other devices at no further cost.

WHAT APPLE ALLOWS, PLAINLY

Apple Maps offers no way to add places to a guide that already exists from outside the app. So the third route produces a new guide holding the old places and the new ones together, which you keep instead of the old one. Wren keeps the places afterwards, so the guide can be made again in a tap if anything goes wrong. A single place is the exception — send one on its own and Maps itself will offer to add it to a guide you already have.

reviewNotes:
WHERE THE IN-APP PURCHASE IS

From a cold start, with nothing added and no account needed:

    1. Open Wren.
    2. Tap the three-dot menu at the TOP RIGHT of the main screen.
    3. Tap "Guides of any size".

That opens the purchase sheet, showing the StoreKit price and an "Unlock for
<price>" button, plus "Restore a previous purchase". This is the only In-App
Purchase in the app: one non-consumable, "Guides of any size", product id
com.spencerfields.littlebird.unlimited.

The same sheet also appears through the features it pays for, if you would
rather reach it that way:

    * Add four or more places, then tap "Make a guide" -- the free tier saves
      three places per guide.
    * Or use "From an existing guide" (step 3 below), which is paid whatever the
      number of places.

The app is iPhone-only (TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY = 1). Your last review ran on an
iPad Air 11-inch, where it runs in iPhone compatibility mode; the menu is in the
same place there.

TESTING THE APP

Tap "Add" at the bottom left. It offers three sources:

    1. "Add screenshots" -- take or save a few screenshots containing place
       names (for example a screenshot of a social post listing restaurants in a
       city) and select them. Wren reads the names on device using the Vision
       framework, asks which city they are in, and finds them using MapKit.
       Tapping "Make a guide" opens Maps with the places in a new guide.

    2. "From a file" -- opens the document picker and reads a list exported from
       another app: CSV, KML, KMZ, GPX, GeoJSON, or a Google Takeout export.
       Each row is looked up with MapKit, aimed at the coordinate in the file
       where there is one. A sample CSV is two lines:
           name,latitude,longitude
           Padella,51.5054,-0.0903

    3. "From an existing guide" -- paste a guide link, which Maps produces via
       Share then Copy Link. Wren decodes the places already in it and shows
       them as a collapsed group. This is the second paid feature.

On point 3, please note: there is no way to add places to a guide that already
exists, so publishing produces a NEW guide holding the old places and the new
ones together. The app says so before publishing, and the App Store description
says so too. It is a limitation of the guide link format, not an attempt to
duplicate anybody's data.

Wren requires no account and no sign-in.

IF YOU WOULD RATHER NOT TRANSACT

There is a complimentary code that unlocks both paid features without a
purchase. Please use it only after looking at the purchase sheet above, because
entering it unlocks the app and the purchase entry then disappears -- there is
nothing left to buy.

Long-press the "Wren" title at the top left of the main screen, then enter:

    7QFG-7FVY-QXP6-2AT6

This entry point is not advertised anywhere in the app and is not reachable by
ordinary users. Codes are issued individually and checked against a server, so a
code cannot be shared onward. This one is not single-use and will keep working
across resubmissions.

A small number of complimentary codes also open a console for issuing and
withdrawing codes, used by the developer. It is reached by the same long press,
and only on a device that has redeemed such a code -- the code above is not one,
so this console cannot be opened during review. It sells nothing and changes
nothing about the app's features.

Entering a code is the only time Wren contacts a server of its own, unless the
code also grants administrative access, which is re-confirmed about once a day.
The code above is not one of those. It sends the code and a random identifier
for the device, nothing else. Everything the app does otherwise happens on the
device.
whatsNew:
Send a screenshot straight to Wren.

Somebody sends you a reel with three places in it. Screenshot it, tap Share, and pick Wren — the places are read the moment it opens. No leaving the app you were in, no going back through the photo picker. Several images at once work too.

That is the whole change. Nothing about how Wren reads a screenshot or builds a guide has moved.
